title: React docs set: React Developer Tools, and Render and Commit
why_trusted: Official react.dev documentation maintained by the React team: 'React Developer Tools' covers the Components and Profiler panels; 'Render and Commit' states a render is triggered by initial render or a state update in the component or an ancestor, and rendering is recursive through children.

title: Performance features reference / overview (Chrome DevTools)
why_trusted: Official Chrome DevTools documentation; its sections 'Observe Core Web Vitals live' and 'Compare your experience to the experience of your users' show live metrics and CrUX field data built into the Performance panel.

title: dequelabs/axe-core
why_trusted: The open-source accessibility rules engine (MPL-2.0, specialised niche: automated web accessibility testing) maintained by Deque Systems; it powers the axe browser extensions and is embedded in Lighthouse, Accessibility Insights for Web, Cypress-axe, Storybook a11y and Jest-axe per the project's own doc/projects.md.
niche_reason: Specialised niche: automated web accessibility testing engines.

title: Redux docs set: Configuring Your Store and Essentials Part 1 (Redux DevTools Extension)
why_trusted: Official redux.js.org documentation. 'Configuring Your Store' (section 'Other options') documents the devTools option; Essentials Part 1 (section 'Redux DevTools Extension') says it shows a history of state changes and supports time-travel debugging. The 'prior art' page links to reduxjs/redux-devtools (MIT, 14.4k stars).

title: Google Search Central: JavaScript SEO basics, Redirects, and Site move with URL changes
why_trusted: Google's own Search Central documentation of how Googlebot crawls, renders and indexes JavaScript pages (rendered HTML, status codes, soft 404, JSON-LD), plus the redirects page (permanent 301/308 vs temporary 302/307, server-side preferred, JavaScript redirects may be missed) and the site-move page ('Avoid chaining redirects': Googlebot follows up to 10 hops; keep chains under 5).

title: W3C WAI: Selecting evaluation tools, Evaluation Tools List, and page-structure tutorials (headings, regions)
why_trusted: W3C Web Accessibility Initiative guidance. 'Selecting Web Accessibility Evaluation Tools' says tools cannot check everything and human judgement is required; the Evaluation Tools List names WAVE; the page-structure tutorials 'Headings' and 'Page Regions' define heading ranks and landmark regions (banner, nav, main, contentinfo).

title: Understanding SC 1.4.3: Contrast (Minimum) (WCAG 2.2)
why_trusted: The W3C Understanding document for the AA contrast criterion: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text; it lists Colour Contrast Analyser as a measuring tool.

title: Anatomy of a WebExtension (MDN)
why_trusted: MDN's WebExtensions reference, maintained by Mozilla, defines manifest.json, background scripts, content scripts, popups and web accessible resources for the cross-browser API.

title: Content scripts (Chrome for Developers)
why_trusted: Official Chrome extension documentation; its sections on isolated worlds, injection methods, run_at and 'Stay secure' define how content scripts touch pages and what permissions injection needs.

title: Content Security Policy (CSP) (MDN)
why_trusted: MDN's reference guide to the Content-Security-Policy header, covering delivery, strict CSP, clickjacking, Trusted Types and report-only testing.

title: RetireJS/retire.js
why_trusted: Widely used open-source scanner (Apache-2.0, 4.2k stars) for JavaScript libraries with known vulnerabilities, with CLI, browser extension, Burp and ZAP integrations.

title: chrome.declarativeNetRequest API reference
why_trusted: The official Chrome extensions API reference for the API that block, redirect and header-modifying extensions use; it defines the rule action types block, redirect, allow, upgradeScheme, modifyHeaders and allowAllRequests, plus rule limits and the Header modification section.
